title: Browser De-Slop: How to Remove Bloatware from Modern Browsers Using Policy Files
summary: The article provides a detailed guide on how to remove unnecessary features and bloatware from modern browsers (Firefox and Chromium-based browsers) using policy files. It includes specific file paths for different operating systems, configuration examples for disabling telemetry, AI-related features, built-in password managers, and other unwanted functionalities. The guide also covers the installation and configuration of uBlock Origin for ad-blocking and privacy protection.
key_points: Modern browsers come with excessive bloatware that can be disabled via settings or policy files.
Policy file locations vary by OS and browser (e.g., `/etc/firefox/policies/policies.json` for Firefox on Ubuntu).
Firefox policy file example disables telemetry, AI features, Pocket, DNS-over-HTTPS, and configures uBlock Origin with specific filter lists.
Firefox settings include disabling search suggestions, setting DuckDuckGo as the default search engine, and blocking tracking cookies.
Chromium policy file example disables telemetry, Google Cloud Print, Chromecast, browser sync, and configures uBlock Origin Lite.
Chromium settings include disabling search suggestions, setting DuckDuckGo as the default search engine, and blocking third-party cookies.
Custom certificate authorities can be added in Firefox via policy files but require workarounds for Chromium.
Policy files enforce settings system-wide, making them ideal for privacy-focused or minimalist browser setups.

reason.details: The article provides a highly detailed, practical, and well-structured guide on removing bloatware from browsers using policy files. It includes accurate technical instructions, OS-specific paths, and configuration examples for both Firefox and Chromium-based browsers. The content is fact-based, with clear distinctions between instructions (fact) and recommendations (opinion). No spam, clickbait, or hidden ads were detected. The category 'OpenSource' is appropriate, and the article maintains a neutral tone while offering actionable advice.
